arxiv-2001-02214.title: Attributed Multi-Relational Attention Network for Fact-checking URL Recommendation Conference: The 28th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; November 3–7, 2019; Beijing, China The 28th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM ’19), N
arxiv-2001-02214.creator: Di You, Nguyen Vo, Kyumin Lee, Qiang Liu
arxiv-2001-02214.description: Abstract . To combat fake news, researchers mostly focused on detecting fake news and journalists built and maintained fact-checking sites (e.g., Snopes.com and Politifact.com). However, fake news dissemination has been greatly promoted via social media sites, and these fact-checking sites have not been fully utilized.

arxiv-2201-11771.title: A spatially-resolved large cavity of the J0337 protoplanetary disk in Perseus Journal: AAS Journals
arxiv-2201-11771.creator: Taichi Uyama, Garreth Ruane, Kellen Lawson, Takayuki Muto, Charles Beichman, Nienke van der Marel
arxiv-2201-11771.description: Abstract We present Keck/NIRC2 K p ​ L p K_{\rm p}L_{\rm p} high-contrast imaging observations of a J0337 protoplanetary disk. The data discover the spatially-resolved large cavity, which is the second report among protoplanetary disks in the Perseus star forming region after the LkH α \alpha 330 system.

arxiv-2204-10856.title: New Core-Guided and Hitting Set Algorithms for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization
arxiv-2204-10856.creator: João Cortes, Inês Lynce, Vasco Manquinho
arxiv-2204-10856.description: Abstract In the last decade, a plethora of algorithms for single-objective Boolean optimization has been proposed that rely on the iterative usage of a highly effective Propositional Satisfiability (SAT) solver. But the use of SAT solvers in Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization (MOCO) algorithms is still scarce.

arxiv-2303-11602.title: Convergence of variational Monte Carlo simulation and scale-invariant pre-training
arxiv-2303-11602.creator: Nilin Abrahamsen, Zhiyan Ding, Gil Goldshlager, Lin Lin
arxiv-2303-11602.description: Abstract We provide theoretical convergence bounds for the variational Monte Carlo (VMC) method as applied to optimize neural network wave functions for the electronic structure problem. We study both the energy minimization phase and the supervised pre-training phase that is commonly used prior to energy minimization.

arxiv-2309-00215.title: Towards Addressing the Misalignment of Object Proposal Evaluation for Vision-Language Tasks via Semantic Grounding
arxiv-2309-00215.creator: Joshua Feinglass, Yezhou Yang
arxiv-2309-00215.description: Abstract Object proposal generation serves as a standard pre-processing step in Vision-Language (VL) tasks (image captioning, visual question answering, etc.). The performance of object proposals generated for VL tasks is currently evaluated across all available annotations, a protocol that we show is “misaligned” - higher scores do not necessarily correspond to improved performance on downstream VL tasks .

arxiv-2312-02341.title: Incentive Systems for Fleets of New Mobility Services
arxiv-2312-02341.creator: Ali Ghafelebashi, Meisam Razaviyayn, and Maged Dessouky
arxiv-2312-02341.description: Abstract Traffic congestion has become an inevitable challenge in large cities due to population increases and expansion of urban areas. Various approaches are introduced to mitigate traffic issues, encompassing from expanding the road infrastructure to employing demand management. Congestion pricing and incentive schemes are extensively studied for traffic control in traditional networks where each driver is a network “player”.

arxiv-2312-11468.title: Bias-Reduced Neural Networks for Parameter Estimation in Quantitative MRI Publication type: PRE-PRINT – SUBMITTED TO MAGNETIC RESONANCE IN MEDICINE
arxiv-2312-11468.creator: Andrew Mao, Sebastian Flassbeck, Jakob Assländer
arxiv-2312-11468.description: Abstract 1 Purpose To develop neural network (NN)-based quantitative MRI parameter estimators with minimal bias and a variance close to the Cramér-Rao bound. 2 Theory and Methods We generalize the mean squared error loss to control the bias and variance of the NN’s estimates, which involves averaging over multiple noise realizations of the same measurements during training.

arxiv-2404-06736.title: New Partial Orders of Polar Codes for BMSC
arxiv-2404-06736.creator: Liuquan Yao 1 , Zhichao Liu 1 , Yuan Li 2 , Huazi Zhang 2 , Jun Wang 2 Guiying Yan 3 and Zhi-Ming Ma 3
arxiv-2404-06736.description: Abstract In this paper, we define partial orders (POs) of polar codes based on the Bhattacharyya parameter and the bit-error probability, respectively. These POs are applicable to arbitrary binary memoryless symmetric channel (BMSC). Leveraging the extremal inequalities of polarization transformation, we derive new POs for BMSC based on the corresponding POs observed in the Binary Erasure Channel (BEC).

arxiv-2408-12618.title: Refining Genetic Discoveries of Group Knockoffs via A Feature-level Filter
arxiv-2408-12618.creator: Jiaqi Gu
arxiv-2408-12618.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jiaqi Gu. Identifying variants that carry substantial information on the trait of interest remains a core topic in genetic studies. In analyzing the EADB-UKBB dataset to identify genetic variants associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD), however, we recognize that both existing marginal association tests and conditional independence tests using existing knockoff filters suffer either power loss or lack of informativeness, especially when strong correlations exist among variants.

arxiv-2501-16922.title: Agential AI for Integrated Continual Learning, Deliberative Behavior, and Comprehensible Models 869
arxiv-2501-16922.creator: Zeki Doruk Erden, Boi Faltings
arxiv-2501-16922.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zeki Doruk Erden, Boi Faltings. Contemporary machine learning paradigm excels in statistical data analysis, solving problems that classical AI couldn’t. However, it faces key limitations, such as a lack of integration with planning, incomprehensible internal structure, and inability to learn continually. We present the initial design for an AI system, Agential AI (AAI), in principle operating independently or on top of statistical methods, designed to overcome these issues.

arxiv-2505-11664.title: A Local Polyak-Łojasiewicz and Descent Lemma of Gradient Descent For Overparametrized Linear Models
arxiv-2505-11664.creator: Ziqing Xu ziqingxu@wharton.upenn.edu, Hancheng Min hanchmin@seas.upenn.edu, Salma Tarmoun starmoun@sas.upenn.edu, Enrique Mallada mallada@jhu.edu, René Vidal vidalr@upenn.edu
arxiv-2505-11664.description: Abstract Most prior work on the convergence of gradient descent (GD) for overparameterized neural networks relies on strong assumptions on the step size (infinitesimal), the hidden-layer width (infinite), or the initialization (large, spectral, balanced). Recent efforts to relax these assumptions focus on two-layer linear networks trained with the squared loss.

arxiv-2507-15147.title: STL-GO: Spatio-Temporal Logic with Graph Operators for Distributed Systems with Multiple Network Topologies CCS: Theory of computation Logic and verification
arxiv-2507-15147.creator: Yiqi Zhao, Xinyi Yu, Bardh Hoxha, Georgios Fainekos, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh, Lars Lindemann
arxiv-2507-15147.description: Abstract . Multi-agent systems (MASs) consisting of a number of autonomous agents that communicate, coordinate, and jointly sense the environment to achieve complex missions can be found in a variety of applications such as robotics, smart cities, and internet-of-things applications. Modeling and monitoring MAS requirements to guarantee overall mission objectives, safety, and reliability is an important problem.

arxiv-2512-07375.title: LUNE : Efficient LLM Unlearning via LoRA Fine-Tuning with Negative Examples
arxiv-2512-07375.creator: Yezi Liu, Hanning Chen, Wenjun Huang, Yang Ni, Mohsen Imani
arxiv-2512-07375.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) possess vast knowledge acquired from extensive training corpora, but they often cannot remove specific pieces of information when needed, which makes it hard to handle privacy, bias mitigation, and knowledge correction. Traditional model unlearning approaches require computationally expensive fine-tuning or direct weight editing, making them impractical for real-world deployment.

arxiv-2606-04396.title: Read the Trace, Steer the Path: Trajectory-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Language Models
arxiv-2606-04396.creator: Anant Khandelwal, Manish Gupta

pmc-11382008.title: A pilot pragmatic randomized controlled trial of a nicotine metabolite ratio-guided smoking cessation intervention in a lung health and screening program
pmc-11382008.creator: Scott D Siegel, Ross Budziszewski, Essie Layton, Brian Nam, Robert Schnoll
pmc-11382008.description: IntroductionPatients with pulmonary nodules detected through lung cancer screening or as incidental findings are often followed in lung health and screening programs. The use of personalized pharmacotherapy for smoking cessation informed by the nicotine metabolite ratio (NMR), a measure of nicotine metabolism, has not yet been evaluated in this setting.

pmc-11460166.title: The industry demand oriented construction of intelligence medicine specialty in traditional Chinese medicine university: teachers’ perspective
pmc-11460166.creator: Wei Lin, Xiaoxue Chen, Yujie Zhang, Yuxiang Fu, Tao Jiang, Lin Xu
pmc-11460166.description: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to explore the relationships between teaching competence, career development, industrial orientation, and specialty construction in the case of intelligent medicine specialties in universities of traditional Chinese medicine, as well as the influencing factors of specialty construction.MethodsTwo-stage sampling with unequal probability was conducted to distribute self-administered questionnaires in the fieldwork.

pmc-11716386.title: The effects of blood‐brain barrier permeability on Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers and their impact on clinical performance
pmc-11716386.creator: Nattanich Pornteparak, Poosanu Thanapornsangsuth, Thanakit Pongpitakmetha, Tatchaporn Ongphichetmetha, Juthamas Rianaree, Watayuth Luechaipanit, Thanaporn Haethaisong, Adipa Chongsuksantikul, Yuttachai Likitjaroen, Thiravat Hemachudha
pmc-11716386.description: BackgroundThe validation of blood‐based biomarkers presents a promising role in Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis owing to their accessibility and diminished invasiveness. However, despite awareness of confounding factors like kidney function, inaccuracies persist in AD diagnosis using plasma p‐tau. Notably, diverse conditions that modify blood‐brain barrier (BBB) permeability have been linked to high plasma p‐tau levels, irrespective of AD pathophysiology.

pmc-12594118.title: Screening-Detected Atrial Fibrillation and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Working-Age Adults
pmc-12594118.creator: Yuichiro Mori, Mitsuaki Sawano, Shun Kohsaka, Yusuke Tsugawa, Motoko Yanagita, Shingo Fukuma
pmc-12594118.description: BACKGROUND:Early detection of atrial fibrillation (AF) is essential for preventing ischemic stroke and other cardiovascular complications. However, the incidence and prognosis of AF in the general middle-aged population remain unclear. In Japan, annual health screenings for employees include mandatory ECGs, offering a unique opportunity to fill this evidence gap.

pmc-13162015.title: Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma with Dual Smooth-Muscle and Osteogenic Differentiation Mimicking Plasma Cell Dyscrasia: A Rare Diagnostic Pitfall
pmc-13162015.creator: Arnav P Rathod, Hrishikesh S Saodekar, Yogesh B Rathod, Rajendra Baitule, Ganesh Pundkar
pmc-13162015.description: Introduction:Pleomorphic sarcoma (PS) is a high-grade soft-tissue malignancy with marked morphologic variability. Divergent differentiation is recognized, but dual smooth-muscle and osteogenic lineage differentiation is exceedingly rare and may mimic other malignancies.Case Report:A 52-year-old male presented with progressive low-back pain, weight loss, and an enlarging iliac mass.

pmc-13188239.title: Prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum coinfection with Schistosoma haematobium and Schistosoma mansoni among children in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13188239.creator: Usama Hassan, Ayesha Siddiqa, Yu Zhu, Jinhong Zhao
pmc-13188239.description: BackgroundMalaria and schistosomiasis are major public health challenges in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), with overlapping geographical distributions leading to high rates of coinfection among children. Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) causes most severe malaria cases, while Schistosoma haematobium (S. haematobium) and Schistosoma mansoni (S. mansoni) are the predominant schistosome species.

pmc-13361162.title: Full Vectorial Field Sensing Using Liquid Crystal Droplet Arrays
pmc-13361162.creator: Xuke Qiu, Jinge Guo, Jiahe Cui, Runchen Zhang, Zimo Zhao, Yifei Ma, Waqas Kamal, Steve J. Elston, Alfonso A. Castrejón‐pita, Stephen M. Morris, Chao He
pmc-13361162.description: Determining the amplitude, phase, and polarization profile of light is essential for both fundamental scientific discovery and applications spanning optical metrology, microscopy, astronomy, and optical communication/computing technologies. However, most modern measurement approaches are unable to retrieve such parameters readily, often relying on bulky and expensive hardware or lacking the capability for single‐shot sensing.

pmc-13408030.title: Real-life experience of tildrakizumab 200 mg in complex psoriatic patients: a case series
pmc-13408030.creator: Giulia Odorici, Cinzia Buligan, Carolina Fantini, Lucia Mantovani, Giulia Rech, Lidia Sacchelli
pmc-13408030.description: Background/ObjectivesThe management of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis may be particularly challenging in patients with a high disease burden and multiple comorbidities. This case series provides real-world evidence on the effectiveness of tildrakizumab 200 mg in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis characterized by clinical factors such as multiple comorbidities, high body weight, involvement of difficult-to-treat areas, and prior therapeutic failures.

pmc-13461714.title: Biomechanical effects of supplemental posterior cervical stabilization in one-to three-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion: a finite element analysis of construct length–dependent stress shielding and adjacent segment mechanics
pmc-13461714.creator: Junwei Zhang, Tairui Zhang, Maji Sun, Yang Sun, Shuo Feng, Jun Sun, Feng Yuan

pmc-13595141.title: Prostate-specific membrane antigen in malignant brain tumors: vascular heterogeneity, imaging promise, and therapeutic challenges
pmc-13595141.creator: Bihani Pokharel, Mingtao Feng, Yuechao Yang, Zhe Qi, Sabrina Shah Kazmi, Yiqun Cao, Liangdong Li, Yang Gao
pmc-13595141.description: Malignant brain tumors have high morbidity and poor prognosis. Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) has emerged as a promising vascular biomarker in this setting, particularly in gliomas and brain metastases. This review synthesizes current evidence on PSMA expression patterns, regulatory mechanisms, imaging applications, and translational potential in malignant brain tumors.

pmc-13676046.title: Retinal AI risk stratification and cardiovascular event yield across QRISK3 categories in UK Biobank
pmc-13676046.creator: Sahil Thakur, Jaewon Seo, Zahra Darmani, Dongjin Nam, Husain Khaki, Simon Nusinovici, Tyler Hyungtaek Rim
pmc-13676046.description: mework works at population scale, but a substantial fraction of future events arises in people below the 10% threshold [[3], [4], [5]]. The practical question for a prevention service is not only who is above a line, but how efficiently a test concentrates true future events among the people it flags.

pmc-13680605.title: An integrated single-cell transcriptomic and microbiome dataset of orbital adipose tissue in thyroid eye disease
pmc-13680605.creator: Xiang Xu, Fei Wang, Weiqi Liu, Haowen Li, Yingyu Wang, Yuan Li, Bing Wang, Mingming Liu, Yang Li
pmc-13680605.description: Thyroid eye disease (TED), also historically referred to as thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO) or Graves’ orbitopathy (GO), is an autoimmune ophthalmopathy characterized by inflammation and adipogenesis within orbital adipose (OA) tissue. While the contribution of immune cell infiltration and fibroblast activation is recognized, the cellular heterogeneity and the potential role of local microbial dysbiosis in the orbital microenvironment remain poorly defined.
